content.text:
Both merged and `main` is synced.

- **[#965](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/965)** → `5f91366` — `pack-version-bumped`: a change under `packs/<id>/` must move that pack's version.
- **[#966](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/966)** → `74098b8` — CI sweeps the work scope on every non-automation branch, with the base fetched and named, the scope printed, and an empty scope treated as an error rather than a pass.

Conversation captured to `conversation-logs` for the growth-extract pass. One incidental confirmation: [#963](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/963), which merged between the two, edited `packs/grow_with_claudinite/` and `packs/sheepdog/` and bumped both versions (1→2, 2→3) — so the invariant now enforced is the one that repo's work already follows.

> ✅ All done — both PRs merged, `main` at `74098b8`. Still open, but not from this work: whether members' own CI should gate the work scope, and #939's candidates (1) atomic packs+engine delivery and (3) the delivery-gate backstop.

input.body:
Refs #939. Found by the probe in [#967](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/967) (closed unmerged), which was meant to red on `pack-version-bumped` and instead red one step earlier.

[#966](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/966)'s guard test ran the work sweep inside the **unit suite** and asserted the real tree came back clean. That makes any branch carrying a finding fail as a *broken test* — wrong layer, wrong message, and one step before the sweep that reports it properly, which also means the sweep never runs to say what is actually wrong.

The verdict belongs to CI. The test now asserts only that the invocation is well-formed: the runner exits 0 or 1 rather than crashing, and a failing exit names what failed.

**Verified on the probe branch**: with this fix and the deliberate violation in place, [run 32076019319](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32076019319) passes the unit step and fails exactly where it should —

```

[BLOCKING] pack-version-bumped  packs/canary-probe/pack.mjs
  this change edits packs/canary-probe/ but leaves its version at 2
1 blocking, 0 advisory (work scope: changed vs origin/main).
```

**The demonstration** — [#967](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/967), one line appended to `packs/canary-probe/README.md` with no version bump. [Run 32076019319](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32076019319) is red at `Conformance sweep (work scope)`:

```
       whole delivery signal, so an edit that does not move it stays in the canon forever
1 blocking, 0 advisory (work scope: changed vs origin/main).
```

Probe PR closed unmerged, with that evidence recorded on it.

**What the probe caught** — the first attempt ([run 32075721661](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32075721661)) went red one step *earlier*, in the unit suite. [#966](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/966)'s guard test re-ran the work sweep inside the tests and asserted the tree was clean, so any branch with a finding failed as a broken test — wrong layer, wrong message, and the sweep never ran to say what was actually wrong. Had I not run this probe, the first real violation would have reported itself as a test failure.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#970](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/970) awaits your LGTM; whether members' CI should gate the work scope too; and #939's candidates (1) atomic packs+engine delivery and (3) the delivery-gate backstop.

content.text:
Here is exactly what the unit suite printed on the probe, before the fix:

```
not ok 146 - the runner answers cleanly in CI's exact invocation against the real tree
  error: 'Command failed: node engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs --changed --base origin/main'
  stack: checkExecSyncError (node:child_process:916:11) …
```

Three concrete costs, none of them about other projects — the file is canon-only (`engine-tests/`):

1. **The finding vanished.** The point of a check here is that its failure message *is* the lesson: "edits `packs/canary-probe/` but leaves its version at 2 — raise it to 3". That text never appeared. What a person saw was a node child-process stack trace, in test 146 of 2099, naming no pack and no remedy.
2. **The run stopped before the step that would have said it.** Steps run in order and the job halts at the first failure, so the work sweep never executed — the entire CI log for that run contained zero information about the actual problem. Red, with nothing to act on.
3. **It fires locally on ordinary in-progress work.** Any session running the suite on a branch that has a work finding — most commonly a commit that hasn't picked up its `Refs #N` yet — gets a failing unit test for a branch state that is simply not finished. That's recurring noise for every session, not just for this class of violation.

What it is *not*: a portability or member-facing issue. Nothing about it ships to other repos.

Whether it's worth a PR of its own is your call — it's six lines. If you'd rather not carry a separate review for it, say so and I'll close [#970](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/970); the cost of leaving it is the three items above, not a broken gate. The gate itself works either way, as [#967](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/967) showed.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#970](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/970) — merge it or tell me to close it; whether members' CI should gate the work scope too; and #939's candidates (1) atomic packs+engine delivery and (3) the delivery-gate backstop.
